ent_technology_series_elastic_actuator_2.name: Series Elastic Actuator
ent_technology_series_elastic_actuator_2.summary: Actuator with an elastic element in series with the motor and load, enabling accurate force control and shock tolerance.
ent_technology_series_elastic_actuator_2.body:
## Overview

A Series Elastic Actuator (SEA) is a joint actuator architecture that places an elastic element (such as a spring) in series between the motor and the output load. It indirectly estimates the output force by measuring the deformation of the elastic element, thereby transforming traditional "position control" into high-precision "force control," while inherently providing impact resistance and energy storage capabilities. What it truly changes is not how the actuator generates force, but rather it converts "force"—a physical quantity that traditionally requires expensive sensors for direct measurement—into a state variable that can be indirectly inferred through inexpensive displacement measurements. ent_tech_on_device_vla_inference.name: On-Device VLA Inference
ent_tech_on_device_vla_inference.summary: The practice of running Vision-Language-Action models directly on robot-embedded edge compute rather than offloading to edge or cloud servers, driven by latency, connectivity, and privacy constraints.
ent_tech_on_device_vla_inference.body:
## Overview

On-device VLA inference refers to deploying vision-language-action models directly on edge computing devices embedded in robots, rather than offloading to edge servers or the cloud, to satisfy latency, connectivity, and privacy constraints. What it truly changes is not the model's accuracy itself, but the upper bound on how quickly a robot can react to the physical world—when the control loop requires end-to-end inference latency below 20 ms, the cost of network round trips becomes unacceptable.

ent_technology_quasi_direct_drive_actuat.name: Quasi Direct Drive Actuator
ent_technology_quasi_direct_drive_actuat.summary: Actuator design using low-ratio gears with high-torque motors to achieve high bandwidth and force transparency.
ent_technology_quasi_direct_drive_actuat.body:
## Overview

A Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD) actuator is a joint actuator architecture that combines a **low gear reduction ratio (typically 3:1–10:1) with a high-torque-density motor**. It sits between direct drive (no gearbox) and high-reduction-ratio rigid actuators: the reduction ratio is low enough that external forces can be "transmitted" directly back to the motor side, so output torque can be estimated simply by measuring motor current, enabling high-bandwidth force control without joint torque sensors. This approach was validated and popularized by the MIT Cheetah series of quadruped robots and is currently one of the mainstream choices for high-dynamic legged and humanoid robot joints.

ent_tech_robogen.name: RoboGen
ent_tech_robogen.summary: An LLM-driven automatic task-generation framework for robotics that proposes tasks and generates simulation code to expand synthetic training data diversity.
ent_tech_robogen.body:
## Overview
RoboGen is a generative simulation framework driven by large language models. Through a self-reinforcing pipeline of "task proposal—scene generation—supervision generation—skill learning," it automatically produces diverse tasks and corresponding simulation code, expanding the diversity of synthetic training data at the task-semantic level. What it truly changes is not "how to generate more simulation data," but "who decides what tasks to generate"—shifting the decision-making power over task distribution from human experts to large models.
